output.reason: A few days of right-hand numbness and tingling worse at night, without reported weakness, facial droop or speech change, suggests a compressive neuropathy needing Counsel clinician assessment and a decision on nerve testing, but no reported feature requires emergency or same-day in-person care.
output.patientMessage: Please start a message review with a Counsel clinician in this thread; hand numbness and tingling worse at night often comes from nerve compression at the wrist, but a clinician should assess it and decide whether nerve testing or treatment is needed. Meanwhile avoid sleeping with bent wrists. Seek emergency care now if you develop new weakness, face droop, slurred speech, or sudden loss of feeling.
differential: Carpal tunnel syndrome (median nerve compression at wrist)
